summary: Join our Environmental Economics and Valuation Techniques course to learn how to assess and value natural resources effectively.
lede: Environmental economics and valuation connect environmental impacts with economic evidence for project and investment decisions. For environmental and sustainability professionals, economists, planners and project teams, the course covers how to define a valuation question, choose market and non-market methods, and assess data, assumptions and uncertainty. Participants also practise presenting valuation findings clearly to support appraisals and decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for a diverse group of professionals who are responsible for justifying environmental decisions and investments.
audience: Economists and planners in government agencies
Natural resource and conservation project teams
Climate finance and adaptation project staff
modules: Foundations of Environmental Economics for Decision-Makers
Ecosystem Services and Natural Capital in Practice
Defining the Valuation Question and Study Scope
Data Planning and Evidence Collection for Valuation
Benefit Transfer and Rapid Valuation Under Constraints
Cost of Environmental Degradation and Policy Appraisal
Integrating Valuation into Business Cases, EIAs/ESIAs, and Investment Decisions
Environmental Economics Tools for Utilities and Resource Pricing
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of economic principles and familiarity with environmental issues. Previous experience in project planning, policy analysis, or sustainability initiatives is beneficial.
